result.document_summary: New Jersey's Fair Chance in Housing Act (P.L. 2021, c.110), which restricts when and how landlords may consider applicants' criminal records and bars drug/alcohol testing of applicants.
result.notes: Single enacted statute. Approved June 18, 2021; section 14 makes it effective the first day of the seventh month next following enactment, computed as January 1, 2022. The Act's drug/alcohol-test ban, advertising limits and enforcement provisions are details of the same instrument and are folded into one screening_restrictions record. The Act does not state its own application-fee rules beyond a disclosure and refund remedy, so no application_screening_fees record is output.

rules.title: Fair Chance in Housing Act: criminal-record screening limits
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or consider an applicant's criminal record before making a conditional offer. After a conditional offer, only certain convictions within set look-back periods may be considered, subject to an individualized assessment, written notice of withdrawal, and an appeal opportunity. Providers also may not require drug or alcohol tests of applicants.
rules.key_value: No criminal-record inquiry before conditional offer; look-back 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree), 1 year (4th degree); serious listed offenses and lifetime sex-offender registration have no look-back limit
rules.quoted_span: A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.coverage_text: Covers rental dwelling units offered for rent by housing providers, other than units in owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.

exemptions.label: Owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units

all_of.text: premises of not more than four dwelling units

rules.exemptions_text: A dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units is not a covered rental dwelling unit.
rules.interaction: Does not bar or affect independent rights or actions, including under the Law Against Discrimination (P.L.1945, c.169). Enforcement is through the Division on Civil Rights rather than court actions.
